title: Public-Anchor Drift Adapters for Privacy-Limited Embedding Model Upgrades

contributions.purpose: Enable privacy-preserving embedding model upgrades without access to in-domain data.
contributions.mechanism: Public-Anchor Drift Adapter (PADA): train a lightweight residual MLP g(x)=x+W2*GELU(W1x+b1)+b2 (hidden dim 256) with a simple MSE objective on paired embeddings from public Wikipedia text, mapping new-model embeddings into the legacy embedding space; no in-domain corpus needed.
contributions.evaluation: Trained on ~5,000 Wikipedia anchor pairs; upgrade scenario all-distilroberta-v1 -> all-mpnet-base-v2 (768-dim) evaluated by nDCG@10.
contributions.domain: Dense retrieval / embedding model upgrades in vector databases (privacy-sensitive deployments)
contributions.source_quote: We propose PADA, a privacy-preserving approach to embedding model upgrades that requires no access to in-domain data.

contributions.purpose: Show public-anchor training matches or exceeds in-domain adapters, supporting the model-pair-specific drift hypothesis.
contributions.mechanism: Compare PADA against an in-domain adapter (same architecture, trained on 5,000 corpus documents) across four BEIR datasets spanning scientific, medical, financial, and argumentative domains.
contributions.evaluation: PADA exceeds in-domain adapter on all four datasets with recovery ratios rho 1.11-1.31 (avg 1.22); nDCG@10 gains of +5.0 (SciFact), +9.8 (TREC-COVID), +7.2 (FiQA), +6.1 (ArguAna); recovers 60-97% of oracle vs 46-84% for in-domain.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that PADA exceeds in-domain adapter performance on four diverse BEIR datasets (scientific, medical, financial, argumentative), supporting the hypothesis that drift is model-pair-specific.

contributions.purpose: Confirm the gains arise from genuine alignment rather than training artifacts.
contributions.mechanism: Shuffled-pair null control that uses the same Wikipedia text and training procedure but with randomly permuted target embeddings.
contributions.evaluation: Shuffled-pair adapter yields near-zero nDCG@10 (~0.000) on all datasets, indistinguishable from the misaligned baseline.
contributions.source_quote: We validate our approach with a shuffled-pair null control that confirms gains arise from genuine alignment rather than training artifacts.

contributions.purpose: Characterize sample efficiency for practical deployment.
contributions.mechanism: Sweep public anchor corpus size Np over {500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000} and measure recovery ratio.
contributions.evaluation: Sigmoid-shaped scaling: negligible below 2,000 pairs (rho<0.17), rapid gains 2,000-5,000, near-saturation at 10,000 (rho 0.89-1.07); recommend >=5,000 pairs.
contributions.source_quote: We characterize sample efficiency, finding that approximately 5,000 public anchor pairs provide meaningful adaptation, with near-saturation at 10,000 pairs.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Following Vejendla (2025), we use a residual MLP architecture that adds a learned correction to the input embedding.

Drift-Adapter (Vejendla, 2025) trains residual MLP, affine, or Procrustes adapters on paired embeddings from the target corpus... Our work demonstrates that a simple MSE-trained adapter using only public text can match or exceed in-domain adapters, eliminating the need for private data access.

This simple MSE objective, without additional geometry-preservation losses used in prior work (Yoon & Arik, 2025; Jha et al., 2025), is sufficient when the underlying drift is approximately smooth across the embedding space.
Our work extends this insight to model upgrades, demonstrating empirically that public anchors can capture the global transformation between embedding spaces.
